subsystems.name: Optical sensor module
subsystems.role: shines light into the finger and measures how much comes back, which rises and falls with each heartbeat.

subsystems.name: Motion sensors
subsystems.role: detect movement and body position for step counts, sleep staging and activity recognition.

subsystems.name: Compute and radio
subsystems.role: filters the raw signals, runs on-device algorithms and sends results to a phone.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: fits days of continuous sensing into a package weighing a few grams.

subsystems.name: Enclosure and fit
subsystems.role: holds the electronics against the artery-rich underside of the finger without pinching it.

buildSteps.title: Pick the sensing site
buildSteps.detail: Engineers model light paths and pressure at the finger base, then fix the LED–photodiode spacing and angles so the signal is strong but the ring stays comfortable.

buildSteps.title: Design the electronics stack
buildSteps.detail: A flexible or rigid-flex printed circuit board is laid out to wrap the finger, with the optical parts on the inner face and the radio and battery elsewhere.

buildSteps.title: Make the optical module
buildSteps.detail: LEDs and photodiodes are mounted with opaque barriers between them so emitted light cannot leak straight to the detector.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the shell
buildSteps.detail: The outer shell and inner moulding are produced — often by metal injection moulding, machining or ceramic moulding — then polished and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in a cleanroom
buildSteps.detail: Electronics are folded into the shell, the battery bonded in, the sensor window sealed and the whole unit pressure-tested for water resistance.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Every ring is characterised so differences in LED brightness and detector sensitivity do not distort the readings.

buildSteps.title: Develop the algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Signal-processing pipelines turn noisy light traces into heart rate, heart-rate variability, breathing rate and sleep stages, validated against lab-grade equipment.

buildSteps.title: Test on people
buildSteps.detail: Wear trials across skin tones, finger sizes, temperatures and activity levels check accuracy and comfort before shipping.

prerequisites.why: cheap, tiny, efficient light sources and detectors make finger-worn sensing possible.
they let a coin-sized device run for days while syncing continuously.

prerequisites.tech: Tiny lithium-polymer cells and wireless charging
prerequisites.why: energy density and recharging convenience are what make a ring form factor practical.
motion data is needed to separate real pulse signals from movement noise and to stage sleep.
optical readings are easily disturbed by motion, cold fingers, tattoos and skin tone, so accuracy remains the hard part.

pathway.milestone: rings that track sleep, heart rate, heart-rate variability, temperature and activity
pathway.unlocks: continuous, low-friction health monitoring people actually keep wearing.

pathway.milestone: clinically validated detection of conditions such as sleep apnoea and atrial fibrillation
pathway.unlocks: wearables becoming regulated screening tools rather than lifestyle gadgets.
better management of cardiovascular and respiratory disease at home.

pathway.milestone: rings linked into medical workflows and remote care
pathway.unlocks: early warning of illness and fewer hospital visits.
